title: Reviewer rotation and load-balancing policy for sustainable per-script review coverage
context: As scheme coverage grows, the review burden on individual qualified per-script reviewers increases. A single-reviewer dependence is a sustainability risk: if the one qualified Devanagari reviewer becomes unavailable, new Devanagari schemes are blocked. Rotation and load-balancing policies ensure the reviewer network is maintained, onboarding of new reviewers is defined, and no single reviewer is a single point of failure.
objective: Write a reviewer rotation and load-balancing policy document (docs/reviewers/rotation-policy.md) defining: how review assignments are distributed across qualified reviewers for a given script, the maximum concurrent assignments per reviewer, how reviewers are onboarded to replace or supplement existing coverage, the escalation path if reviewer availability drops below minimum for a script, and the cadence for roster review.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/reviewers/rotation-policy.md defines review assignment distribution: assignments rotated across qualified reviewers for a script; maximum concurrent assignments per reviewer specified
Policy defines the minimum reviewer coverage per script (at least 2 qualified reviewers active for each script with a released scheme) and an escalation path if coverage drops below minimum
Policy defines the onboarding process for adding a new reviewer to replace or supplement existing coverage: same qualification criteria as reviewers-001, shadow review before solo sign-off
Policy defines the cadence for roster review (e.g., every 6 months): confirm reviewers are still active and available, update roster.yaml
Policy is reviewed and approved by the steward and maintainer; linked from docs/reviewers/README.md
resources: PLAN.md — Sustainability & maintenance; Governance; Risks (no qualified reviewer for a script)
output: docs/reviewers/rotation-policy.md; updated docs/reviewers/README.md linking the policy
